question.problem: Given that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ evaluate ${f}_{yxy}(1,\frac{\pi }{2})$ if ${f}_{yy}(x,y)=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).$
question.worked_solution:
As the higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yxy}(x,y) & ={f}_{yyx}(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{yy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-2x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+(-{x}^{2})\cdot (-y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+{x}^{2}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
{f}_{yxy}(1,\frac{\pi }{2})=-2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(1\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})+(1)^{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(1\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})=\frac{\pi }{2}\,\,
$$
